abstract: The World Broadcasting Unions (WBU)i Technical Committee is addressing an increased number of issues as broadcasting, on a worldwide basis, has entered into a more complex, challenging era, exemplified by massive spectrum competition, rapid regulatory and technology changes, and a more threatening cyber environment.

authors.bio: John Lee is the chairman of the World Broadcasting Unions’ (WBU) Technical Committee as well as the chairman of the North American Broadcasters Association (NABA)’s Technical Committee’s Cyber Security Sub-Committee. He is currently a digital engineering consultant working for several large organizations. Previously, he was executive director, Technology Solutions, for CBC/Radio-Canada, Canada’s national public broadcaster, where he served for 38 years. In this role, he was responsible for engineering services, including digital television and radio transmission facilities, satellite and telecommunications networks, and for IT, including mobility services, UC, applications, information security and governance.
authors.name: John Lee

authors.bio: Morwen Williams is the director of U.K. Operations for BBC News, leading the technical and studio teams of BBC News. She is responsible for creative technical news gathering as well as all news studios in London and Salford at Media CityUK and editing in London—a team of more than 700 people.She is the chair of the World Broadcasting Unions (WBU) International Media Connectivity Group, working with other broadcasters to find common solutions in this area. She is an alumni of the Media Transformation Challenge at Harvard University’s Kennedy School. She is a keen supporter of the BBC’s apprentice schemes to deliver new and more diverse technical talent in the BBC, as well as working with BBC News Women in Technology programme. She’s been a mentor for RISE Women in Broadcasting and the John Schofield Trust for young journalists. She is proud to have been RISE Women in Broadcasting Woman of the Year in 2019.
authors.name: Morwen Williams
